# Recording is simulated and the Transcript is generated by an LLM

A Fireflies clone implies audio capture and speech-to-text. This project has neither. The brief allows recording to be a placeholder and budgets under ten hours, and the only API credential available is Anthropic's. So a Recording is a timer with a start, an end, and a duration; when it stops, Claude generates a speaker-attributed, timestamped Transcript from the Meeting's title, Speakers, and optional agenda.

Transcript production sits behind a `TranscriptionProvider` interface with two implementations: the Claude generator and a deterministic fake used by every automated test. A real speech-to-text vendor (Whisper, Deepgram) would be a third implementation plus audio capture in the client; nothing else would change.

**Considered**: browser Web Speech API (free, but Chrome-only and flaky, no speaker labels), MediaRecorder upload to a speech-to-text vendor (needs a new paid vendor, audio storage, and roughly a third of the time budget). Both rejected as poor robustness-for-cost on a reviewer's machine that may have no microphone.
